adjudicated.jp: 適当に部室で暇を潰して、教室に戻る途中。
adjudicated.en: After suitably passing time in the club room, I'm on my way back to the classroom.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator kills time casually or aimlessly in the clubroom. 'Suitably passing time' suggests propriety or adequacy and is not idiomatic for this adverbial nuance.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'After killing some time in the clubroom,'

adjudicated.jp: 人気のない廊下で、処女がうずくまっていた。
adjudicated.en: A maiden was crouching in a corridor devoid of human presence.
comments: Pun not as obvious in English I'm afraid. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Maiden can carry a virginal meaning, but it is an archaic euphemism that softens the source's blunt comic label.
adjudicated.remedy: Use a blunt contemporary term for virgin.

adjudicated.jp: 「大丈夫ですか、お嬢さん？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Is everything well, ojou-san?"
comments: Formal. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The ordinary address 'miss' or 'young lady' is left as an unexplained romanized Japanese expression inside otherwise English dialogue.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Are you all right, miss?'

adjudicated.jp: 尻に手を伸ばす。
adjudicated.en: I extended my hand towards her behind.
adjudicated.assessment: The hand reaching toward her rear is accurately conveyed with a mild euphemism.

adjudicated.jp: 「おっとぉ！」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Woh'tt'ooo!"
adjudicated.assessment: The surprised 'Whoa!' is rendered as an opaque apostrophe-heavy spelling that supplies no readable English pronunciation or meaningful source distinction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use an elongated 'Whoa!'

adjudicated.jp: 瞬発力を発揮して、少女は立ち上がった。
adjudicated.en: In a display of explosive force, the girl stood straight up,
adjudicated.assessment: The girl's explosive quickness in springing upright is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: すり足で距離を取る。
adjudicated.en: and gained distance with a suri-ashi.
comments: Specific judo technique, that is the correct English term. This is pretty clever for Miki, but still not Unreset clever. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Suri-ashi is a real sliding martial-arts step and fits the combat posture. The problem is leaving the technique unexplained in otherwise English prose and attaching it awkwardly to an indefinite article.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe the sliding or shuffling step in accessible English.

adjudicated.jp: 臨戦態勢に移行するのが早い。
adjudicated.en: She's quick to transition into combat readiness.
adjudicated.assessment: Her rapid transition into a combat-ready stance is accurately conveyed in matching mock-technical diction.

adjudicated.jp: しかも跳ね起きると同時に、俺に一撃を加えてきた。
adjudicated.en: And, simultaneously with her springing up, she inflicted an attack on me.
comments: Rag below. Still sharp enough to mask some of her later behavior. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She strikes the narrator as she springs up. The nominalized timing phrase and 'inflicted an attack' are unidiomatic calques that obscure a simple simultaneous blow.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'As she sprang up, she struck me.'

highlights.text: simultaneously with her springing up, she inflicted an attack

adjudicated.jp: 「……なかなかやるな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...nice one there, very nice."
adjudicated.assessment: The impressed acknowledgment of her skill is naturally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「せんぱいこそ」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Same to you, Senpai."
adjudicated.assessment: Her reciprocal compliment to the senior is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 片手で受け止めた、顔面を狙って放たれた雑巾を、静かに床に落とす。
adjudicated.en: The rag that she threw towards my face fell from the one hand I had caught it with to the floor, in silence.
comments: See CCD5001. This is a move he learned from Taichi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator deliberately and quietly drops the rag he caught. The English makes the rag fall from his hand and turns controlled action into an accidental event inside a malformed relative construction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I quietly dropped the rag I'd caught in one hand.'

highlights.text: fell from the one hand I had caught it with

adjudicated.jp: 「そですね」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "It has."
adjudicated.assessment: In context, the casual agreement that it has been a while is naturally supplied.

adjudicated.jp: 映画化された某有名ファンタジー小説のヒロインみたいな少女が、立っている。
adjudicated.en: This girl so like the heroine of that famous fantasy novel adapted to the big screen stands up.
comments: I sooo wanted this not to be Hermione from Harry Potter, if only because first film is from 2001 and would mess up the dating in a way that would force me to consider that Taichi would only have read the book, despite it having been released in the US the damn same month the VN takes place in and the translation to Japanese being Dec 1999, which admittedly is one of the earliest translations... but CCZDXC confirms it. Personality-wise, it does fit in many ways, especially that part near the end of book 3. If it helps, Wikipedia reports that Hermione was named from Shakespeare, further cementing things. What Johnson has to do, however, I still only have the vaguest idea. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The girl is standing there and resembles the heroine of a well-known fantasy novel adapted for film. The English is grammatically malformed and changes the static description into the action of standing up.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'A girl resembling the heroine of a famous fantasy novel turned movie stood before me.'

highlights.text: This girl so like the heroine of that famous fantasy novel adapted to the big screen stands up.

adjudicated.jp: 安心していい。外見だけだ。
adjudicated.en: Be at ease. That's just her looks.
comments: Actually, Hermione does fit the Genius Loli archetype nearly to a tee. Or she would if she weren't surrounded by people the same age. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The reassurance that the resemblance is only superficial is retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「しばらく会ってないからって名前とか忘れてへんで？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Would it be strange if I said that we haven't met in a long enough while that I forgot your name and the like?"
adjudicated.assessment: The source assures her that he has not forgotten her name merely because they have not met for a while. The English reverses this into a hypothetical confession that he did forget it.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It's not like I forgot your name just because we haven't seen each other for a while.'

highlights.text: Would it be strange if I said that we haven't met in a long enough while that I forgot your name and the like

adjudicated.jp: 「やー」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Naaah."
comments: Think about it for a second: Miki'd have no problem with Taichi forgetting even her name. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The drawn-out casual rejection is effectively conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「だから安心してくれ……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ah, but be at ease..."
adjudicated.assessment: The continued request that she relax is substantively retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「せめて女性の名前で」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "At least use a girl's name."
comments: The first thing to notice is that she's complaining he's not using a girl's name when making up a name for her, not that he's doing so in the first place. Miki knows that forgetting even important stuff is normal for Taichi.

As for the reference itself, no one in the Harry Potter cast is named "Johnson", so that looks like a dead end; maybe the Johnson & Johnson baby shampoo, with its iconic yellow color - see CCA0027 for Coppertone, so it's not alone. This *may* be a reference to Robert Johnson, see CCC3002. This would fit as an early-bird spoiler. The only other I can think of is http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrienne_Johnson_Kiriakis (notice the KIRIakis, so very Japanese-sounding though it isn't), given the Adrian/Adrienne vs. Alien, see CCZAS. But that's really really reaching. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The plea to use at least a female name is accurately rendered.

adjudicated.jp: 外人なのはもういい、という顔をしていた。
adjudicated.en: A face one could say had had enough of being thought foreign.
comments: Ah, there we get deep into the Nations of the World metaphor. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her expression of being fed up with the foreigner assumption is accurately conveyed despite stiff syntax.

adjudicated.jp: 「腕をあげたな、美希」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You've improved your skills, Miki."
comments: More ambiguity: Miki already seems better than she should be. At this point it should just be trickery, but since there's no certainty that this is the very first week, it's not impossible that with the above lack of surprise at the memory loss, that Miki already knows Taichi has "reset", and therefore is not quite aware of all that he taught her in the weeks before. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The acknowledgment that her skill has improved is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「ええ」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Yep."
adjudicated.assessment: The affirmative response is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 山辺美希は涙を誘うほど乏しい胸を張った。
adjudicated.en: Yamanobe Miki stuck out a chest so unplentiful it invites tears.
comments: See CCA0009B: she DOES have boobs that he doesn't expect. This loli flatness vanishes around Kiri's route, never to return. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The joke describes a chest so meager it brings tears. 'Unplentiful' is an unnatural and weak adjective that obscures the blunt visual insult.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'a chest so meager it could move you to tears.'

adjudicated.jp: 「わたしのお尻は高いですから」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Because my behind is valuable."
comments: Not yet "because I hold myself precious", but suspiciously close. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her claim that access to her rear comes at a high value is naturally captured.

adjudicated.jp: 「ちょっと触れたけどね」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Although I managed just to graze it."
adjudicated.assessment: The qualification that he touched it slightly is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「サービスです」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Fanservice."
comments: Going with technical term due to imitative behavior. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: In context, rendering the deliberately provided glimpse as fanservice is functionally apt.

adjudicated.jp: 動じない。
adjudicated.en: Unperturbed.
adjudicated.assessment: Her lack of agitation is exactly conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「だがそのスカートのめくれまでは……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But until I flip that skirt..."
adjudicated.assessment: The fragment refers to the skirt having flipped up, continuing a bluff about what just happened. The English makes it a future deliberate action by the speaker.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'But your skirt did flip up—'

adjudicated.jp: 「めくれてません（きっぱり）」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "You shan't flip. (Decisevely)"
comments: ... (silence) -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She firmly states that the skirt did not flip up. The English instead commands a future subject not to flip, omits the skirt, and misspells the manner note.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It didn't flip up. (Firmly.)'

adjudicated.jp: やるな。
adjudicated.en: Not bad.
adjudicated.assessment: The impressed internal acknowledgment is naturally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: ハッタリもきかなくなったか。
adjudicated.en: Bluffs are no longer effective, then?
comments: See Mi(yu)ki. Those were largely threats. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The realization that bluffs no longer work is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「いいだろう。今回は花を持たせておく」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "But it's fine. For this once, I'll let you carry the flowers so that you can take credit for this."
comments: Literal and lateral due to overlap with the nickname. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The line ultimately explains that the other person may take the credit, so the source meaning is recoverable. Retaining the literal flower image before redundantly glossing it produces awkward, nonidiomatic dialogue.
adjudicated.remedy: State naturally that the other person may have the credit or glory this time.

adjudicated.jp: 「えへ」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Eheh!"
adjudicated.assessment: The pleased little vocalization is reasonably recreated.

adjudicated.jp: にっこりと笑った。
adjudicated.en: She smiled brightly.
adjudicated.assessment: The bright smile is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: うわー、抱きしめてぇ。
adjudicated.en: Waaah, hug meee!
comments: Supposing he wants to be held back. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator exclaims that he wants to hug her. The English turns that desire into a command or plea for someone else to hug him, reversing the action's direction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'God, I wanna hug her.'

adjudicated.jp: 「なにしてたんだ？　掃除ごっこか？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Watcha doing? Playing cleaning lady?"
adjudicated.assessment: The teasing question about pretending to clean is naturally retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「あ、はい、なんかここんとこ汚れてて」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Ah, yes, things are a bit dirty lately."
adjudicated.assessment: Her explanation that the area has been dirty lately is conveyed with only mild generalization.

adjudicated.jp: 「あっし、きれい好き」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Me, ah' like 'em clean."
comments: Dagnabbit. Supposing the dirty words and dirty thoughts, not so much the dirty corridor. Though if it IS Kiri's blood due to her period... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The exaggerated nonstandard self-presentation as someone who likes cleanliness is recreated through marked English speech.

adjudicated.jp: 架空の力こぶを作る。
adjudicated.en: She flexes an Imaginary bicep.
comments: NOT the bicep polishing gesture, as far as GIS claims. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The imaginary flexed bicep is accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「自発的にかい、そいつはクールだネ！」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "All of your own initiative, that is very cool yes!"
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-praise asks whether she did it voluntarily and calls that cool. The English is a fragment followed by an unnatural declarative tag, losing the question's shape.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'All on your own initiative? That's very cool!'

highlights.text: All of your own initiative, that is very cool yes

adjudicated.jp: 「……あーあー……アレですか」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "...ahh, yeah... that one, yes."
comments: Ah, this scene is unclear. -GHSoHelpful
adjudicated.assessment: The hesitant recognition of what he means is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんか久々ですねえー」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Really been a long while there."
adjudicated.assessment: The casual observation that it feels like a long time is recognizable, but the English omits a subject and finite auxiliary and appends an unnatural 'there.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It really has been a while, hasn't it?'

highlights.text: Really been a long while there

adjudicated.jp: なんとも切なそうな顔をする。
adjudicated.en: She makes a face that looks very pained.
adjudicated.assessment: Her intensely pained expression is accurately described.

adjudicated.jp: 二回も思ってしまったぞ。
adjudicated.en: I even thought that twice dammit.
adjudicated.assessment: The self-aware complaint that he thought it twice is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 焦ってはいかん、冷静に対処するのだ。
adjudicated.en: Getting flustered is a no go, cope with this with composure.
adjudicated.assessment: The instruction to handle the situation calmly is accurate in content, but the repeated preposition and clinical 'cope' produce an unidiomatic calque.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Don't panic. Handle this calmly.'

adjudicated.jp: 酸いも甘いも噛みわけたエリートヤングアダルト候補生として！
adjudicated.en: Like an elite cadet of young adulthood who is experienced in the ways of the world, having tasted both its bitter and its sweet!
comments: Boy this will return. Literal and lateral because uhmmm science. -GHScience
adjudicated.assessment: The grandiose self-description and bitter-and-sweet experience idiom are expansively but accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「どどどどどどうしたことだ、山辺君！　そんなに嫌であれば無理に余白を潰そうなんて思わないぞ！　正直に申告するのダっ！？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Wh-wh-wh-wh-wh-what is wrong, Yamanobe-kun?! If that is so disagreeable, than I shall not even think to wast that blank space! I proclaim this with honesty, see?!"
comments: Blank space of the notebook I guess. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker commands her to report her feelings honestly. The English changes the addressee's required confession into the speaker proclaiming his own honesty; surrounding spelling and conjunction errors further damage the line.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Tell me honestly!'

adjudicated.jp: 声震えまくり。
adjudicated.en: My voice just shakes.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says his voice is trembling violently or all over, not merely that it shakes. The English drops the emphatic degree and shifts into an oddly generic present.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'My voice was shaking like crazy.'

adjudicated.jp: 「おお、泣いてる、あわわ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ohhh, she's crying, ahWahWah!"
comments: It may be because she's annoyed at how many damn times she's done this in previous weeks outside the loop; but it may be that she is, genuinely, sad that this hasn't happened in a while and simply doesn't understand how to correctly express this emotion. In this sense, she's just like Taichi. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The alarmed realization that she is crying is retained with matching flustered noise.

adjudicated.jp: 目尻をぬぐう。
adjudicated.en: She wipes the corners of her eyes,
adjudicated.assessment: The wiping at the corners of her eyes is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: 俺もつられて泣きそう。
adjudicated.en: which carries me to tearfulness as well.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator feels like crying in sympathy. 'Carries me to tearfulness' is an abstract and nonidiomatic rendering of emotional contagion.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Now I feel like crying too.'

adjudicated.jp: 「あ、いえ、なんでもありません、サー」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Ah, no, it's nothing, SAH!"
adjudicated.assessment: Her reassurance and exaggerated English-style address are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「涙腺からちょっと、青春汁が、漏れて……」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "It's just that my lachrymal glands leaked some adolescent juice..."
comments: 汁 juice, it's a crying cross. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-anatomical joke about adolescent fluid leaking from the tear glands is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「なんだ……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Whoa..."
adjudicated.assessment: The deflated reaction is acceptably conveyed in context.

adjudicated.jp: 青春汁か。
adjudicated.en: Adolescent juice then.
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated coined expression is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「驚かすない」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Don't scare me then."
comments: He's absolutely unfazed by the nonsense that is "eyes leaking adolescent juice". He doesn't seem to understand the point of tears at all. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The childish command not to scare him is functionally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 冷や汗をぬぐった。
adjudicated.en: I wiped off cold sweat.
adjudicated.assessment: The action is clear, but English requires a possessive or determiner for the sweat being wiped away; the bare mass-noun construction reads as a calque.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I wiped the cold sweat from my brow.'

adjudicated.jp: 「じゃあ今回は王子（俺）のサインはおあずけだな」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Well then, this time the Autograph of the Prince (me) is postponed."
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-prince persona says she will have to wait for his autograph this time. The nominalized passive and arbitrary capitalization are not natural English dialogue.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Then you'll have to wait for your prince's autograph.'

highlights.text: the Autograph of the Prince (me) is postponed

adjudicated.jp: 「いえ！」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "NO!"
adjudicated.assessment: The emphatic refusal is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 喉のかすれるような悲鳴。
adjudicated.en: A shriek as if her throat was hoarse.
adjudicated.assessment: The hoarse, strained quality of the scream is conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「いります！　してください！」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "I need you in this! Do this please!"
comments: "I need it" + "put it in" & "please do it" + "please do me". This is another overreaction; Miki just doesn't seem capable of taking things in proper measure, which is why he takes Taichi's Settei so damn seriously. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: She says she wants the autograph and asks him to do it. The English instead says she needs him 'in this,' inventing an object relationship and producing an unintelligible request.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I want it! Please do it!'

adjudicated.jp: 「そ、そんなにしてほしいのかね？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Y, you want this done to you that badly?"
comments: Still puns. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The startled question about wanting it that badly is preserved, including the comic ambiguity.

adjudicated.jp: こっちがたじろぐ。
adjudicated.en: Faltering from my direction.
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator says he is the one who recoils or falters. The English removes the person as subject and substitutes a direction, leaving a sentence fragment.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Now I was the one who recoiled.'

adjudicated.jp: 「してください、してください」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Do this please! Do this please!"
comments: Same as above. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated plea is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 甲高い声で『してください』と連呼される。
adjudicated.en: I'm repeatedly called to "do this please" with a shrill voice.
adjudicated.assessment: He is subjected to the shrill repetition of the quoted plea. 'Called to do this please' converts the words into an indirect summons and is not grammatical English reporting.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She kept shrilling, Please do it, over and over.'

adjudicated.jp: 下腹部が熱くなってきた。
adjudicated.en: The lower abdomen grew hotter.
comments: See CCD0021, it's probably the clearest. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The contextually understood body part is the narrator's own lower abdomen. The English turns it into a generic anatomical object and loses the personal bodily reaction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'My lower abdomen was getting hot.'

adjudicated.jp: どうしてだろう？
adjudicated.en: But why, really?
adjudicated.assessment: The comic question about why is retained.

adjudicated.jp: どうしてなんだろう？
adjudicated.en: For what reason, even?
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated baffled question is preserved through variation.

adjudicated.jp: かいめんたいはいつもぼくの意志をむしして、あばれるんだ―――
adjudicated.en: Why must the erectile tissue of this innocent young boy ignore my volition and just rage---
comments: Adapted boku again, see CCD4003 for more (you know you want). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-innocent complaint about erectile tissue defying his will and acting up is accurately recreated.

adjudicated.jp: 童話調に思考しても生々しさは消えなかった。
adjudicated.en: I may have thought this in the tone of a fairy-tale, but the graphicness didn't go away.
comments: see CCA0007. Break out that On Fairy-Tales essay! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The contrast between fairy-tale framing and persistent visceral immediacy is retained, but 'graphicness' is an awkward abstract coinage that does not naturally express 生々しさ here.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'the visceral reality of it didn't go away.'

adjudicated.jp: 「わ、わかった、ではアレを」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I-, I got that, well then 'that' I'll do."
comments: Break out that "On 'that' I'll do" essay! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The stammered acceptance and turn toward the euphemistic 'that' are visible, but the English is syntactically inverted and over-completes the source fragment with an awkward 'I'll do.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'O-okay. Then, that...'

highlights.text: I-, I got that, well then 'that' I'll do.

adjudicated.jp: 「はい」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Here!"
comments: Break out that "On Here" essay! -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: In the immediate handoff context, the short affirmative is reasonably rendered as 'Here.'

adjudicated.jp: 美希は垂直な胸元をまさぐって、メイトブックを出した。
adjudicated.en: Miki groped about her perpendicular chest, then produced her MateBook.
comments: CURSED YE SHALL BE WITH THE CLIFFENING!!! -AkihaTohno -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The action and the deliberately geometric joke about her chest are both preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 当校では身分証明書をかねるこの手帳を、そう呼ぶ。
adjudicated.en: So it is called at this school, this ID booklet with a second role.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says that this notebook, which doubles as identification, is called that at the school. 'An ID booklet with a second role' reverses which function is being specified and leaves the other role unexplained.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'That's what our school calls this notebook, which doubles as an ID.'

highlights.text: So it is called at this school, this ID booklet with a second role.

adjudicated.jp: そう。
adjudicated.en: Yes.
adjudicated.assessment: The emphatic confirmation is adequately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: どうも本校のお歴々は、『都会』の駅裏にある人気ＮＯ１高級浴場『メイトブック』の存在を知らないようなのだ。
adjudicated.en: No dignitary of this school would be unaware of the existence of MateBook, the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station.
comments: This will be one of the weirdest running gags in the VN. The MateBook will be repeatedly said to be named (or not) after a possible whorehouse, SoapLand or public bathhouse. The origin will change pretty much every time. The point, of course, is that this is part of Taichi's Settei and its origin changing constantly and without warning is the reading key to watch out for other things to. Clarified as it's not necessarily obvious in English that being behind the train station is a popular spot, not a seedy one. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the school's leading figures apparently do not know of the bathhouse. The English reverses that into a claim that none could be unaware, and also invents a 'popular spot' not present in the location phrase.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Apparently, the school's grandees don't know about MateBook, the number-one luxury bathhouse behind the station in the City.'

highlights.text: No dignitary of this school would be unaware of the existence of MateBook, the high-class bathhouse #1 in popularity located in the popular spot behind the main City's train station.

adjudicated.jp: 会員になると手帳を渡され、一回ご利用するごとに姫のスタンプがもらえる。
adjudicated.en: A notebook is given on gaining membership, and for every use a Princess Stamp is received.
comments: Can't source the euphemism, if it even is one. See CCC0000: Ichiko would of course leave a princess stamp... -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The membership booklet and stamp received with each use are accurately described despite stiff passive phrasing.

adjudicated.jp: スタンプを集めることによって、Ｗやトリプルなどのサービスが格安で楽しめるという寸法だ。
adjudicated.en: The accumulation of stamps is the measure of how cheaply one can enjoy services such as the Double or the Triple.
adjudicated.assessment: Collecting stamps enables discounted access to the named services. The English instead makes the number of stamps a measure of relative cheapness, changing the mechanism into a scale.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Collect enough stamps and you can enjoy services like the Double or Triple at a steep discount.'

highlights.text: The accumulation of stamps is the measure of how cheaply one can enjoy services such as the Double or the Triple.

adjudicated.jp: ……トリプルだなんて。
adjudicated.en: ...what's even a triple now.
comments: See CCC4007, though there's another in CCD3003B. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source reacts in astonishment to a triple, while the surrounding context also wonders what realm a triple belongs to. The English is awkwardly interrogative, but the curiosity is not unsupported.
adjudicated.remedy: Render the astonished fragment and ensuing curiosity in natural English.

adjudicated.jp: それはいかなる世界なのか。
adjudicated.en: What kind of world would be that?
adjudicated.assessment: The question's content is correct, but its English word order is unidiomatic.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'What kind of world would that be?'

highlights.text: What kind of world would be that?

adjudicated.jp: 桃源郷なのか。
adjudicated.en: Would it be Shangri-la?
comments: "A permanently happy land, isolated from the outside world", reminds Wikipedia. IOW, endless sex with Miki and Kiri in this Cross World. Remember that extra scene in Kagetsu Tohya, Flower of Thanatos? That's all that needs to be said then. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Using 'Shangri-La' for the imagined earthly paradise is a functional cultural equivalent.

adjudicated.jp: 勃ってきました……。
adjudicated.en: I have erected...
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the speaker is becoming erect. 'I have erected' makes him the transitive agent of an unstated object and is not idiomatic English for the bodily state.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I'm getting hard...'

adjudicated.jp: いかん。
adjudicated.en: This is bad!
adjudicated.assessment: The terse recognition that the situation is bad is naturally conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: ここで安易に前傾シフトをとれば、美希にばれる。
adjudicated.en: If I take a gentle forwards Shift here, Miki will notice.
adjudicated.assessment: The risk of giving himself away by casually leaning forward is retained, but 'take a gentle forwards Shift' is an unnatural mechanical calque and the capitalization is unjustified.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'If I casually shift forward now, Miki will notice.'

adjudicated.jp: 美希は処女だが、男の生理には精通している。
adjudicated.en: Miki might be a literal maiden, but she is acquainted with male physiology,
adjudicated.assessment: Might be can operate concessively rather than expressing real uncertainty. The remaining defect is the archaic literal maiden and the weak rendering of being thoroughly versed in male physiology.
adjudicated.remedy: State plainly that she is a virgin but knows male physiology well.

adjudicated.jp: 俺が教えたから。
adjudicated.en: because I explained it to her.
adjudicated.assessment: The explanation that the speaker taught her is substantively preserved by saying he explained it to her.

adjudicated.jp: 前傾しなくともばれるだろうが、堂々としていれば、格好だけはつく。
adjudicated.en: Even if I don't lean I'll likely be spotted, but if I stay confident, I should at least look cool.
comments: No, that's never cool you damn unrepentant beta. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says brazenly acting as though nothing is wrong will at least preserve appearances. 'Stay confident' and 'look cool' turn that social cover into self-confidence and attractiveness.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She'll probably notice even if I don't lean forward, but if I brazen it out, I can at least keep up appearances.'

highlights.text: if I stay confident, I should at least look cool

adjudicated.en: Miki: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent response is faithfully represented.

adjudicated.jp: あ、今ちらっと見た。
adjudicated.en: Ah, she glimpsed right then.
adjudicated.assessment: The source observes that she just stole a glance. 'Glimpsed' is used transitively without an object and 'right then' weakens the immediate 'just now.'
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Ah, she just glanced over.'

adjudicated.jp: 美希、やや赤面。
adjudicated.en: Miki's face goes fairly red.
adjudicated.assessment: The slight blush is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: なにも言わない。
adjudicated.en: She says nothing.
adjudicated.assessment: Her silence is exactly conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 視線を窓の外に向けて、わずかにもじもじする。
adjudicated.en: She turns her gaze towards the outside via the window, and fidgets slightly.
comments: Is she embarrassed or horny? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The action of looking out the window and fidgeting slightly is present, but the route-like phrase 'towards the outside via the window' is not natural visual description.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She turns her gaze out the window and fidgets slightly.'

highlights.text: towards the outside via the window

adjudicated.jp: うわ、かえって恥ずかしい。なにか言えや。
adjudicated.en: Wah, this is even more embarrassing! Say something!
comments: The damn M. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The increased embarrassment and impatient demand that she say something are naturally preserved.

adjudicated.jp: いっそ言葉で俺を玩弄してくれ。
adjudicated.en: Please make sport of me with words instead!
adjudicated.assessment: The request that she toy with or mock him verbally is accurately preserved in intentionally heightened diction.

adjudicated.jp: 羞恥のあまり、荒ぶる破壊神は鎮まっていく。
adjudicated.en: But the embarrasment is so great that this savage god of destruction grows subdued.
comments: Of course there's a god in here. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The metaphorical content is retained, but 'embarrassment' is misspelled in the displayed prose.
adjudicated.remedy: Correct 'embarrasment' to 'embarrassment.'

adjudicated.jp: 実戦経験がないためか、直で面すると弱いんだな。
adjudicated.en: As a consequence of a lack of combat experience, perhaps, direct confrontation is a weakness.
comments: His dick and Miki both. Remember, she's a Witch of Words. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source infers that she is weak when confronted directly, perhaps because she lacks practical experience. The English depersonalizes her into the abstract claim that confrontation itself is a weakness and places 'perhaps' unnaturally.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Maybe because she has no practical experience, she's weak when faced with the real thing.'

highlights.text: As a consequence of a lack of combat experience, perhaps, direct confrontation is a weakness.

adjudicated.jp: 直ハラ禁止だ。
adjudicated.en: Directassment prohibited.
comments: I know. But mine has the word "ass" in it, so it's automatically better. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The compact English coinage functionally recreates the source's clipped harassment pun.

adjudicated.jp: というか全部、完璧に、申し分のない、痴漢行為である。
adjudicated.en: Or should I say that they all are flawlessly unquestionably molestation.
adjudicated.assessment: The conclusion that all the listed acts are unequivocally molestation is present, but the stacked adverbs are unpunctuated and 'are ... molestation' is not grammatical count syntax.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Or rather, every last one is a perfectly unambiguous act of molestation.'

highlights.text: Or should I say that they all are flawlessly unquestionably molestation.

adjudicated.jp: 「美希は手帳だいぶ使いこんでるなあ。ぼろぼろだ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You've been using this notebook thoroughly, Miki. It's all worn!"
adjudicated.assessment: The source observes that she has used the notebook heavily and that it is in tatters. 'Using ... thoroughly' is an unnatural calque, and 'all worn' weakens the physical condition.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'You've really put this notebook through its paces, Miki. It's falling apart.'

adjudicated.jp: 「ぼろぼろ」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "All worn."
comments: Will return. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated description of the notebook as worn out is adequately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 無意味に繰り返すことで肯定する美希。
adjudicated.en: Miki assents by meaninglessly repeating my words.
comments: See CCD4002B -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her pointless repetition as a form of assent is accurately described.

adjudicated.jp: ページを繰ると、メモ欄にはすでに俺のサインがでかでかと書かれていた。
adjudicated.en: Flipping the pages, I see annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature.
comments: No one else's, meaning it's their game. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The surrounding pages can support a collective or repeated sense for the signature. The confirmed defect is the uncontrolled annotation-fields construction and unnatural large-sized diction, which obscure the large signature already present in the memo space.
adjudicated.remedy: Describe the conspicuously large signature already written in the memo space in natural English.

highlights.text: annotation fields filled with my large-sized signature

adjudicated.jp: 何ページにも渡っている。
adjudicated.en: I pass by several pages.
adjudicated.assessment: The source says the oversized signature extends across several pages. The English instead describes the narrator moving past pages, changing both subject and action.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'It stretched across several pages.'

adjudicated.jp: 俺のサインをコレクトしているかのようだ。
adjudicated.en: It's as if she were collecting my signatures.
adjudicated.assessment: The impression that she is collecting his signatures is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 正確には、俺がコレクトさせているわけですが。
adjudicated.en: Or, to be precise, this is me making her collect them.
comments: Possibly either. It's their game. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The self-correction that he is making her collect them is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 白紙を見つけ、そこに新たなサインを書き込む。
adjudicated.en: I find a blank page and there I fill out a fresh signature.
adjudicated.assessment: The action of finding a blank page and adding a new signature is present, but English speakers write or sign a signature rather than 'fill out' one.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I find a blank page and write a fresh signature on it.'

adjudicated.en: Taichi: "..."
adjudicated.assessment: The silent pause is faithfully represented.

adjudicated.jp: 「あのさ、今回は俺がサインしたくて美希の胸を借りたってことで……全然いじわるしようとか思ってないからね？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You know, this little game of ours here was just because I wanted to put my autograph on your chest padding... not because of mean intent, OK?"
comments: Oh dear. Word itself means "practice with a sparring partner of higher skill", with the implication of imitative behavior; this form means "to have a contest with you"/"challenge you"; and literally it's "borrowed your chest". All necessary. Left vague, because it is after all. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker proposes framing the incident as borrowing her chest because he wanted to sign, then denies intending to tease her. The English invents a shared 'game,' changes the object into padding, and turns the strained excuse into a different proposition.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Look, let's just say I borrowed your chest because I wanted somewhere to sign this time... I wasn't trying to be mean, okay?'

highlights.text: this little game of ours here was just because I wanted to put my autograph on your chest padding

adjudicated.jp: 「嫌がってないですってば」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "I'm telling you I didn't dislike it."
adjudicated.assessment: Her insistence that she did not mind the act is accurately retained.

adjudicated.jp: 「そ、そう？」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "You-, don't?"
adjudicated.assessment: The stammered response is simply 'R-really?' or 'I-is that so?' The English instead forces a grammatically broken negative echo of the previous sentence.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'R-really?'

adjudicated.jp: サインを書き終える。
adjudicated.en: I finished writing my signature.
comments: fucking kanji amirite amirite -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The completion of the signature is accurately stated.

adjudicated.jp: 美希はおだやかな顔をしていた。
adjudicated.en: Miki was making a tranquil face.
adjudicated.assessment: The calm expression is understood, but 'making a tranquil face' is an unnatural English calque for wearing or having that expression.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Miki wore a peaceful expression.'

adjudicated.jp: 確かに嫌がっている風ではない。
adjudicated.en: There's certainly not a whiff of pretense of having disliked it.
comments: This is basically screaming the reading key for the Misato scenes, that 'wind' needs to be read 'pretense'. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source says she certainly does not look displeased. The English instead denies any pretense of having disliked it, shifting from her apparent feeling to whether that feeling is feigned and producing the opposite logical structure.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'She certainly doesn't look bothered.'

highlights.text: There's certainly not a whiff of pretense of having disliked it.

adjudicated.jp: 他のページをざっと調べる。
adjudicated.en: I quickly check out the rest of the pages.
adjudicated.assessment: The quick check through the other pages is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「あー、別にデートの約束とか書いてないんで」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Ah, I don't really write my dating plans or anything there."
comments: It's not her World Domination plans, either. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her casual assurance that no date arrangements are written there is substantively preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「あっそ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Ah well."
adjudicated.assessment: The curt, dismissive acknowledgment is functionally represented.

adjudicated.jp: 手帳を返す。
adjudicated.en: I return the notebook.
adjudicated.assessment: The notebook's return is exactly conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: スリッパの底みたいな胸元に抱きかかえて、
adjudicated.en: She holds it against a chest so like the bottom of a slipper.
adjudicated.assessment: The action and insulting comparison of her chest to a slipper sole are accurately preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「ご安心ください。美希は処女でございます～」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Please be at ease. Miki most certainly is still a virgi～n!"
comments: This is so funnier in the console version where we are reassured that Miki is a girl. Wow, she's not a trap? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mock-formal reassurance and drawn-out final word are both recreated.

adjudicated.jp: 「べ、別にそんなことで安心したりしないもん」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "It-, it's not like you need to reassure me of such things!"
comments: Intentional -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker protests that this fact does not make him feel relieved. The English instead tells her that she does not need to reassure him, changing the subject and the force of the embarrassed denial.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I-it's not like that makes me feel relieved or anything!'

highlights.text: it's not like you need to reassure me of such things

adjudicated.jp: うろたえると俺、小児化。
adjudicated.en: Flustered, I regress to childhood.
comments: He just wrote the blandest tsundere line ever and then called it childish, I just love this stuff. I'm adapting those blatantly badly written lines as parodies of generic bad VN translations, if it's not clear. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The compressed self-observation that fluster makes him regress into a child is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 「はいはい、わかっております」
adjudicated.en: Miki: "Yes, yes, I do understand."
adjudicated.assessment: The indulgent assurance that she understands is naturally retained.
